item.title: Escambia County Fire Rescue Marks National Fire Prevention Week With Battery Safety Focus
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Fire Rescue is joining the nationwide observance of National Fire Prevention Week, running October 4-10, with this year's emphasis on safe charging practices for lithium-ion batteries found in everyday electronics. The week's theme—"Charge into Fire Safety: Safe Charging is a Superpower"—highlights the often-overlooked risks of…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Fire Rescue is joining the nationwide observance of National Fire Prevention Week, running October 4-10, with this year's emphasis on safe charging practices for lithium-ion batteries found in everyday electronics.

The week's theme—"Charge into Fire Safety: Safe Charging is a Superpower"—highlights the often-overlooked risks of improperly charging smartphones, power tools, laptops, toys, and other devices. According to the fire department, damaged or misused lithium-ion batteries can overheat, catch fire, or even explode, making safe habits essential for home safety.

Fire Rescue recommends charging devices on hard, flat surfaces like tables or desks rather than soft surfaces such as beds or couches, which trap heat and block airflow. Larger batteries in power tools, e-bikes, and outdoor equipment should be charged outside when possible. Residents should use manufacturer-approved chargers—cheap or off-brand alternatives may not meet safety standards—and look for certification marks from testing labs like UL, ETL, or CSA on packaging. Once fully charged, devices should be unplugged promptly, as leaving them plugged in can stress batteries and increase overheating risk.

If a device begins to swell, smoke, or emit a strange odor, residents should immediately stop using it. Old lithium-ion batteries should be recycled at certified locations, which can be found through Call2Recycle.org. National Fire Prevention Week, sponsored by the National Fire Protection Association since 1922, is the longest-running public health and safety observance in U.S. history, with presidential proclamations backing the annual event since 1925.

item.title: Senate Democrats block Moody's fraud enforcement bill
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody's effort to establish a National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice hit a roadblock this week when Senate Democrats blocked the legislation, according to a press release from Moody's office. The bill would create a dedicated federal division tasked with investigating fraud schemes and recovering…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody's effort to establish a National Fraud Enforcement Division within the Department of Justice hit a roadblock this week when Senate Democrats blocked the legislation, according to a press release from Moody's office.

The bill would create a dedicated federal division tasked with investigating fraud schemes and recovering taxpayer dollars. Moody, a Florida Republican, introduced the legislation the day after it passed the U.S. House and framed the vote as a partisan divide over fiscal responsibility.

"Combatting fraud should be a 100-0 issue," Moody said in a statement. "Acting as good stewards of taxpayer dollars is the most foundational aspect of being a public servant, yet we continue to battle a party that seemingly wants to protect institutional grift."

According to Moody's office, the administration has uncovered more than $260 billion in fraud nationwide. Moody serves on the Senate Anti-Fraud Task Force, which focuses on identifying federal fraud vulnerabilities and advancing accountability reforms.

item.title: Sgt. Angelique Parker Named Escambia County October Employee of the Month
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Sgt. Angelique Parker, Lead Environmental Enforcement Officer with the county's Natural Resources Management Department, has been selected as Escambia County's October 2026 Employee of the Month. The county recognized her with a proclamation at the Board of County Commissioners meeting on October 1st. Parker is marking a significant milestone this…
item.content:encoded:
Sgt. Angelique Parker, Lead Environmental Enforcement Officer with the county's Natural Resources Management Department, has been selected as Escambia County's October 2026 Employee of the Month. The county recognized her with a proclamation at the Board of County Commissioners meeting on October 1st.

Parker is marking a significant milestone this month—20 years of service with Escambia County as of October 2nd. In her role overseeing code enforcement officers, she handles site inspections for environmental violations, issues citations, prepares cases for hearings, and ensures her team completes required training through the Florida Association of Code Enforcement. She herself holds multiple certifications in code enforcement fundamentals, administrative practices, officer safety, and legal issues.

Natural Resources Management Director Chips Kirschenfeld highlighted Parker's stabilizing presence and respectful approach with residents, especially when handling contentious situations. "She has numerous qualities that benefit the Code Enforcement Division and Escambia County," Kirschenfeld said, adding that her collaborative efforts have improved both internal processes and customer service.

Parker said she's honored by the recognition and proud of the work her department does for county residents. "After 20 years with the county, I can honestly say I am proud of the work we do and the people I have had the privilege of working alongside," she said.

item.title: Ensign Group expands into Florida with nine nursing facilities, including Pensacola-area operations
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The acquisition brings 831 skilled-nursing beds under Ensign's management at locations spanning from…
item.content:encoded:
The Ensign Group, a national nursing and rehabilitation operator, is making a major push into Florida by taking over nine skilled-nursing facilities across the state in a single transaction, according to reporting from the National Atlanta Star.

The acquisition brings 831 skilled-nursing beds under Ensign's management at locations spanning from Pensacola to Jacksonville, Central Florida, and the Gulf Coast. The move represents a significant expansion for the company in the Southeast and marks Ensign's entry into Florida's competitive healthcare market.

Ensign Group operates rehabilitation and nursing facilities across multiple states. The company's entrance into Florida adds to the growing consolidation trend in the skilled-nursing sector, where larger operators have increasingly acquired regional chains and independent facilities over the past several years.

The Pensacola area is among the markets where Ensign will now operate under this expansion. Details on the specific facilities involved and the timeline for the transition were not immediately detailed in the initial announcement.

item.title: Scott, Moody Introduce Bill to Protect Eglin Gulf Test Range from Drilling
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senators Rick Scott and Ashley Moody have introduced legislation this week aimed at safeguarding the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range from potential interference, according to a press release from Scott's office. The Protecting Florida's Offshore Military Readiness Act seeks to preserve the range's use as a military testing ground while the…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senators Rick Scott and Ashley Moody have introduced legislation this week aimed at safeguarding the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range from potential interference, according to a press release from Scott's office. The Protecting Florida's Offshore Military Readiness Act seeks to preserve the range's use as a military testing ground while the Department of Interior explores potential offshore drilling lease sales in the Gulf of America.

The Eglin range, located off the Florida coast, provides critical air, sea, and joint testing and training capabilities for U.S. military operations. Scott emphasized in the release that protecting the range is essential to maintaining American military readiness, while Moody called it "a national military asset that can't be replicated anywhere else in the country."

The bill comes as the Trump administration pursues expanded energy production in the Gulf. According to the senators' statement, the legislation would codify previous protections for the range, allowing uninterrupted access for military operations while the administration pursues its energy dominance goals. The senators argue that American energy expansion can proceed without compromising this unique military resource.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport is rolling out a new convenience today that lets TSA PreCheck members with valid memberships escort travelers to the gate or greet arriving passengers without needing a boarding pass.

The program, called Gateside by TSA PreCheck, is designed to give families and friends more time together at PNS. Eligible visitors can now pass through security checkpoints and access gate areas, making it easier to say goodbye to departing travelers or welcome people home.

According to the City of Pensacola, the move brings PNS in line with similar programs at other airports nationwide. Visitors will need an active TSA PreCheck membership to participate. The program is available starting today.

item.content:encoded:
The Northview Chiefs' homecoming celebration in Bratt ended in disappointment Thursday night as the Destin Sharks dominated in the second half to secure a 35-21 victory.

Destin struck first, scoring a touchdown and field goal to grab an early 10-0 lead. Northview answered back, however, and took a 14-10 halftime advantage heading into the break.

The Sharks outscored the Chiefs significantly after intermission to put the game out of reach. The loss drops Northview's record as the football season continues into October.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County Fire Rescue has determined that stray embers from an outside fire sparked a residential blaze on Muscogee Road in Cantonment Thursday afternoon. Firefighters responded to the scene around 2:40 p.m. and brought the fire under control. The incident underscores the importance of properly monitoring and containing outdoor fires, particularly in residential areas where embers can travel and ignite nearby structures.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Foley has adopted a new ordinance establishing regulations for door-to-door solicitation, according to a city news release reported by WKRG News 5. The Foley City Council voted to approve the measure, which creates new requirements that commercial solicitors must follow when visiting residential areas.

The ordinance aims to establish clearer guidelines for solicitation activity in the city, though specific details about the new requirements were not immediately available. The move reflects growing efforts by municipalities across the region to balance residents' preferences for privacy and safety with legitimate commercial activity.

item.title: Pensacola health clinics preparing for Medicaid changes affecting immigrant eligibility
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The changes are expected to affect how local clinics serve their patient base, though details on the specific timeline and scope of the…
item.content:encoded:
Community health clinics in Pensacola are bracing for operational and financial impacts as shifts in Medicaid eligibility rules for certain immigrant populations take effect, according to reporting from WEAR-TV.

The changes are expected to affect how local clinics serve their patient base, though details on the specific timeline and scope of the eligibility modifications remain in development. Health care providers in the area are working to understand how the policy adjustments will influence their operations, staffing, and ability to serve uninsured or underinsured patients.

Clinics across Pensacola and the surrounding region have historically served immigrant communities, and leaders are assessing what additional resources or alternative care pathways may be needed to maintain continuity of service. The full impact of the eligibility changes could reshape how local health care systems approach preventive care, emergency services, and chronic disease management in communities most affected by the policy shift.

More details on the specific timing and implementation of the Medicaid changes are expected to be clarified in the coming weeks.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

The case drew significant attention across North Florida and the broader Gulf Coast region, as it involved a deputy-involved shooting that resulted in a…
item.content:encoded:
A jury has found former Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office deputy Eddie Duran not guilty of manslaughter in the May 2024 shooting death of Air Force Airman Roger Fortson, according to WKRG News 5.

The case drew significant attention across North Florida and the broader Gulf Coast region, as it involved a deputy-involved shooting that resulted in a fatality. The jury's verdict concludes the manslaughter charge against Duran following the incident at Fortson's Fort Walton Beach home.

Details surrounding the circumstances of the shooting and the jury's reasoning behind the acquittal were not immediately available. The case had been closely watched by law enforcement observers and community members concerned with use-of-force policies.

item.title: Okaloosa County Completes Paving of Nearly 200 Miles of Dirt Roads
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Okaloosa County commissioners announced Thursday that they have paved nearly all county-maintained dirt roads—about 200 miles total—ahead of schedule, thanks to a voter-approved infrastructure surtax passed in 2018. The project, which began as a modest "50 in 5" initiative by then-Commissioner Nathan Boyles in 2020, exceeded its original goal of…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County commissioners announced Thursday that they have paved nearly all county-maintained dirt roads—about 200 miles total—ahead of schedule, thanks to a voter-approved infrastructure surtax passed in 2018.

The project, which began as a modest "50 in 5" initiative by then-Commissioner Nathan Boyles in 2020, exceeded its original goal of stabilizing 50 miles in five years. Instead, the county completed 180 miles of work in just four years, leaving only a handful of roads remaining. The improvements use a limerock base with either chip-seal or hot-mix asphalt topping.

"These are the types of projects that the residents expect from their government," said County Board Chairman Trey Goodwin in a statement. Officials say the paved roads will reduce long-term maintenance and fuel costs that previously went toward repairing washed-out dirt roads after heavy rain. Boyles, now a state representative, praised the county's continued investment in infrastructure. "As a taxpayer, I am proud that our County continues to wisely invest taxpayer money in infrastructure that makes our lives better," he said.

The county maintains a dashboard tracking current and completed infrastructure projects at myokaloosa.com/bcc/infrastructureprojects.

item.title: Walton Area Chamber Announces Keynote Speakers for Oct. 26 Business Conference
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Walton Area Chamber of Commerce is gearing up for its annual "The Next BIG Thing" conference on October 26th at the Hilton Sandestin Beach Golf Resort and Spa, with a lineup of three keynote speakers and nine breakout sessions designed to draw entrepreneurs and business leaders from across the region. The all-day event, presented by Ascension…
item.content:encoded:
The Walton Area Chamber of Commerce is gearing up for its annual "The Next BIG Thing" conference on October 26th at the Hilton Sandestin Beach Golf Resort and Spa, with a lineup of three keynote speakers and nine breakout sessions designed to draw entrepreneurs and business leaders from across the region.

The all-day event, presented by Ascension Sacred Heart Emerald Coast and Eglin Federal Credit Union, typically draws more than 250 attendees. The morning kicks off with Captain Kerry Titheradge, an international television personality and founder of Yachting Concepts LLC, who will speak on personal development and breaking out of comfort zones. Brian Franklin, co-founder and CEO of Vows & Speeches, will deliver the lunch keynote on finding your calling despite setbacks. Laura Quick, founder of Good Grit Magazine, will close the day discussing how mental health and personal growth impact leadership and business performance.

Attendees can choose from breakout sessions organized into three tracks: Leadership Development, Entrepreneurship, and Women in Business. The full-day experience includes breakfast with networking opportunities, complimentary professional headshots, lunch, and a closing cocktail hour with heavy hors d'oeuvres. Throughout the day, raffle prizes totaling thousands of dollars will be available to participants. For more information, contact Ali Weil at 334-328-1568 or ali@weilhousecreative.com.
